{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-md-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"1a758d23dc08d769955b3260179ea51f7757d7fd1b0a968c919a54c3a62683ad","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-md-class-c:lineage:42","source_registry_sha256":"fac6b4b22cda98085a5d7df11947d7cc05865e6c877c17be3df4d573863d1518","source_liveness_sha256":"43fe3511474bec2a914f5cdb112291b78f4339942c4d6fb903d9e3bae34bb3fc"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Crashes and traffic stops","heading":"C — Crashes and roadside emergencies: what to do at the scene, leaving-the-scene penalties, unattended property and safe places","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Crashes and roadside emergencies: what to do at the scene, leaving-the-scene penalties, unattended property and safe places

FACT_ID: sec10-F01 | anchor: A43
After any crash, switch on your emergency flashers or set out flares to warn other drivers. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec10-F02 | anchor: A43
If anyone is hurt in a crash you are involved in, pedestrians and cyclists included, you must stay at the scene. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec10-F03 | anchor: A43
At an injury crash, call 911 at once and report how many people are involved, what injuries they have and where the crash is, and leave the vehicles where they are. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec10-F04 | anchor: A43
A conviction for leaving the scene of a crash with serious injury means your license is revoked. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec10-F05 | anchor: A43
Leaving the scene of a serious-injury crash can also bring up to 5 years in prison and a fine of up to $5,000. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec10-F06 | anchor: A43
Leaving the scene of a crash in which someone dies is a felony punishable by up to 10 years in prison and a fine of up to $10,000. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec10-F07 | anchor: A43
If nobody is hurt but your vehicle cannot be driven, call 911 right away, give the location and say there are no injuries but you need police help. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec10-F08 | anchor: A43
While waiting with a vehicle that cannot move, be patient, keep away from traffic, and do not try to cross the road or stop cars. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec10-F09 | anchor: A43
If nobody is hurt and your vehicle can move, pull it off the road as near to the crash spot as you can to protect people and avoid backups. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec10-F10 | anchor: A43
Swap details with each other driver: name, address, phone, plate number and state, license number, vehicle make and model, and insurance. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec10-F11 | anchor: A43
Ask any witnesses for their names, addresses and phone numbers. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec10-F12 | anchor: A43
Note the crash location, date and time, number of vehicles, and weather and road conditions, and write them down if you can. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec10-F13 | anchor: A43
Record the vehicle damage in writing and photos if possible, and write down how the crash happened. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec10-F14 | anchor: A43
You must always call the police when someone is injured, when a vehicle cannot be moved, or when a driver seems to be under the influence of alcohol or drugs. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec10-F15 | anchor: A44
You must also call the police when a driver has no license, when a driver tries to leave without giving insurance and other details, or when public property is damaged. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec10-F16 | anchor: A44
If you hit an unattended vehicle or other unattended property, stop as near the spot as you can without blocking traffic more than needed. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec10-F17 | anchor: A44
Then try to find the owner to explain and give your information, and if you cannot, leave a note with what happened and your contact details where it will be easily found. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec10-F18 | anchor: A44
If your vehicle hits and injures a domestic animal, such as a dog, cat, horse or cow, you must call the police right away. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec10-F19 | anchor: A44
In any roadside emergency, size up the situation, use good judgment and keep watching traffic, because conditions can change instantly. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec10-F20 | anchor: A44
People are hurt or killed every year at the roadside while waiting for help, so move a disabled vehicle to the shoulder if you can. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec10-F21 | anchor: A44
Reaching an off-ramp or parking lot is worth it even on a flat tire or at the cost of a rim, because more distance from traffic means more safety. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec10-F22 | anchor: A44
Never stop or park in the painted triangular area where an exit ramp splits from the road. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec10-F23 | anchor: A44
If you can stay in the vehicle, keep your seat belt on and face forward so the vehicle's safety features protect you if you are hit. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec10-F24 | anchor: A44
If staying inside is unsafe, choose the safest moment to get everyone out, move quickly away from the road rather than standing by the car, and get behind an embankment, barrier or guardrail. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec10-F25 | anchor: A44
Once out of the vehicle, move to higher ground if you can, face oncoming traffic and stay alert for a car veering toward you. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0044]

Glossary: unattended property — a parked vehicle or other property with no one present [A44]. Domestic animal — a tame animal such as a dog, cat, horse or cow [A44]. Felony — the serious class of crime that leaving a fatal crash scene falls into [A43].
Memory aid: injured, immovable or impaired means call the police [A43].
Misconception: after an injury crash you do not clear the vehicles from the road; you leave them in place, while an injury-free movable vehicle should be moved off the road [A43].
